trust_decision.summary: Which content types the Celery worker will deserialize from broker messages (and, by default, from stored results) is decided by the global CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT setting in relate/settings.py, which at the pinned commit still accepts pickle although tasks are sent as json.

landing_point.why: The summary names Celery pickle deserialization; the only Celery serializer config in the tree is the celery-config block in relate/settings.py, loaded via app.config_from_object at relate/celery.py:18.

fix_sites.entry_point: Celery worker consuming messages from CELERY_BROKER_URL (celery worker -A relate); app configured from Django settings at relate/celery.py:18

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the single global setting governs both task and (by default) result decoding, so there is nothing for a solver to dismiss.
O6_input_shapes: broker task message with content-type application/x-python-serialize (pickle)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An explicit CELERY_RESULT_ACCEPT_CONTENT listing pickle next to CELERY_RESULT_SERIALIZER, so results read by course/views.py:1388 (monitor_task AsyncResult) still decode pickle after accept_content is fixed.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at relate/settings.py:317-318 shows the maintainers already handled result serialization separately from task serialization, so a separate result accept list is plausible; still a config-line sibling, i.e. where-type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An app.conf.update(accept_content=[...pickle...]) or a per-task serializer='pickle' on a shared_task in course/tasks.py:34, overriding the Django setting.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Celery apps often add conf overrides next to config_from_object; but it would be a one-line where-type plant with no mechanism to understand.

O9_family: Insecure deserialization (CWE-502): Celery/kombu accepting pickle content from the message broker

O10_build.toolchain: uv / pyproject (Django, celery 5.6.2, kombu 5.6.2, django-celery-results 2.6.0 per uv.lock)
services: message broker (amqp/redis) for a real worker; tests can use in-memory transport or CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_tasks.py (runs tasks eagerly with CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER, no serializer/accept-content coverage); tests/test_views.py imports relate.celery.app

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove 'pickle' from CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT, which is also the published fix, so the obvious first fix is complete.

out_of_scope_notes: Django cache backends (memcached etc., local_settings_example.py:53-58) pickle cached values used by course/content.py:1186 and the django-cache result backend (relate/settings.py:334); that is Django's own cache design, not this Celery accept-content protection.
local_settings_example.py:142 shows djcelery_email CeleryEmailBackend as an option; the package is not a dependency in pyproject.toml, so it is not followed.
unverified: repo_mb not measured; tiny_repo not assessed.
That Celery 5.6.2 result_accept_content defaults to accept_content (so result decoding in course/views.py:1388 is covered by the same fix) is library behaviour, not checked in this tree.
